system_description.narrative_title: Renewed US–Iran hostilities shock oil and financial markets
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid escalation of US–Iran military strikes has reopened a regional conflict corridor, driving sharp moves in oil, bonds and equities while raising the risk of wider Middle East contagion. The episode functions as an open system: kinetic actions, sanctions/blockades and political messaging feed into oil supply perceptions and market volatility, which in turn influence diplomatic postures and domestic politics (notably US election calculus). International institutions (UN, IAEA), neighbouring states and market participants are external inputs that modulate system behavior and feedback loops.
system_description.scope: Kinetic exchanges between the US and Iran, regional state responses (Gulf states, Israel, Hezbollah, Syria, Lebanon), disruptions to Hormuz and Gulf oil flows, global oil pricing and trading, financial market reactions (equities, bonds, FX, crypto), sanctions/blockade measures, diplomatic and informational maneuvers by governments and international bodies.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil supply and trading system
International financial markets (equities, bonds, FX, digital assets)
Middle East regional conflict dynamics (Israel-Gaza, Hezbollah, Syria, Lebanon)
International diplomacy and institutions (UN, IAEA, EU/NATO responses)
evidence_headlines: Global oil prices surge to a 6-week high after the U.S. strikes Iran in Hormuz
US launches new strikes on Iran and Tehran hits back in widening conflict
U.S. crude near $90 as Iran retaliates with strikes on Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain
U.S. Stocks Fall as Oil Surges After New Middle East Strikes
Trump aides, fearing a midterm rout, push to keep Iran war 'quiet' for now

variables.name: Kinetic strike intensity
variables.description: The aggregate rate and severity of armed strikes and kinetic military actions occurring within the regional conflict corridor.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: The overall severity and scope of economic restrictions, trade limits and financial penalties applied to actors connected to the conflict.

variables.name: Trade blockade intensity
variables.description: The extent to which physical or de facto blockades impede commercial shipping and export routes in the region.

variables.name: Maritime flow disruption
variables.description: The degree of interruption to seaborne energy and commodity transit through key chokepoints and shipping lanes.

variables.name: Perceived crude oil supply availability
variables.description: Market and stakeholder beliefs about current and near‑term availability of crude oil relative to expected demand.

variables.name: Energy inventory levels
variables.description: Quantities held in strategic and commercial oil and refined‑product stocks that can be deployed to buffer supply shocks.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The market price per barrel for benchmark crude grades, representing current commodity valuation.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short‑term variability and uncertainty in oil prices as measured by realized or implied volatility metrics.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: The realized or expected variability across broad financial markets, including equities, bonds and FX, reflecting systemic uncertainty.

variables.name: Bond yield level
variables.description: Average yields on traded sovereign and high‑quality debt instruments that reflect interest rate expectations and risk premia.

variables.name: Equity valuation level
variables.description: Aggregate market valuations of equity indices or broad equity market capitalization relative to fundamentals.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The prevailing tendency of market participants to prefer safe assets over risky assets, influencing asset allocation and flows.

variables.name: Capital flow volumes
variables.description: The net flows of investment capital across asset classes and borders responding to risk, returns and policy signals.

variables.name: Diplomatic signaling intensity
variables.description: The frequency, clarity and forcefulness of public and private diplomatic communications and informational campaigns related to the conflict.

variables.name: Regional contagion risk
variables.description: The assessed probability that localized hostilities will spread to additional actors, geographies or supply nodes in the region.

variables.name: Monetary policy tightness
variables.description: The extent to which monetary authorities are adopting restrictive policy settings (rates, liquidity operations) that affect financial conditions.

catalysts.title: Continued U.S. strikes campaign
catalysts.description: Sustained U.S. kinetic campaign against Iran with further targeted strikes and waves of operations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: “US military says it completed latest wave of strikes on Iran”; “US launches further strikes on Iran”.

catalysts.title: Iran retaliatory strikes continue
catalysts.description: Ongoing Iranian strikes on neighboring states and regional targets in response to U.S. actions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: “Iran retaliates with strikes on Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain”; “Iran strikes Kuwait”.

catalysts.title: Maritime incidents in Strait of Hormuz/shipping lanes
catalysts.description: Attacks, interdictions or insurance shocks affecting commercial shipping and tanker transits through Hormuz and adjacent lanes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: “Oil Prices Rise as Renewed U.S.-Iran Fighting Deepens Hormuz Supply Risks”; “Hormuz” surge headlines.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ output decision (likely unchanged)
catalysts.description: OPEC+ meeting where output policy is expected to be kept unchanged despite Middle East disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: “OPEC+ likely to keep oil output policy unchanged on Sunday.”

catalysts.title: IAEA board push to refer Iran to UN Security Council
catalysts.description: Diplomatic action at the IAEA board to escalate Iran to the UN Security Council, raising pressure and signalling.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: “US and allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council, diplomats say.”

catalysts.title: Sustained blockade stalls Iran oil exports
catalysts.description: Continuation or intensification of a de facto blockade that keeps Iranian crude off the market.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: “Blockade succeeds where sanctions failed as Iran oil exports stall.”

catalysts.title: Possible post-midterms intensification of attacks
catalysts.description: U.S. campaign or allied operations may intensify after U.S. midterm elections, per internal signals.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: “attacks may intensify after November elections”; “Trump aides… push to keep Iran war 'quiet' for now.”

catalysts.title: Outcome of US probe into wedding strike
catalysts.description: Findings or public statement from US investigation of the reported wedding strike could alter policy and signaling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: “US probes Iran wedding strike”; “Vance: US probing airstrike that Iran says hit a wedding party.”

catalysts.title: EU contribution to Lebanon mission
catalysts.description: European countries move to contribute forces or support to a Lebanon mission, affecting regional containment.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: “More than 10 EU countries willing to contribute to Lebanon mission.”
